trajectory_summary: The call opens with an atypical, talkative customer who frames the interaction as one comparison-shopping data point among several vendors, for a non-standard home-occupancy/nonprofit property. The rep steadily pulls the conversation back into the standard verify-and-book structure, holds scope reasonably well on pricing/packet requests, but drifts into some premature system-design reasoning (ground mount vs. northern building) that belongs to the specialist stage. The call ends with a clean day+time booking, making this a mixed-shape call: real structural discipline wins alongside a few scope and follow-up gaps.

primary_coaching_focus.why: On a complex, non-standard property, the rep is most tempted to start solving the layout problem herself. This call is the clearest example on the floor of a rep drifting into specialist-tier system design talk (mount type, which building gets panels) instead of just capturing raw property facts for the design team.

key_moments.stewart_read: The customer describes a mixed-use property (educational/event space plus household occupancy, LLC moving toward nonprofit) that doesn't cleanly fit Ion's standard single-family-homeowner qualification flow. The rep gets a 'home occupancy' answer and moves on without probing whether this is treated as residential or commercial for underwriting/install purposes.

key_moments.stewart_read: Customer names grid reliability in a mountain area as a driver — a resilience/backup-power motivator that could map to battery interest. Rep does not reflect this back or connect it to any backup solution.

key_moments.quote: So so here's what I'm thinking, Benjamin. So what it sounds like you're wanting to do is, like, a ground mount system. Is that right?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep begins reasoning through system layout (ground mount vs. roof) with the customer in real time — this is design-tier content that belongs to the specialist's proposal call, not the scheduler's verify call.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. Exactly. So we'll need to we don't do the groundnuts here at ION, so we'll primarily focus on that Northern building.
key_moments.stewart_read: Two distinct things happen in one line: stating Ion doesn't install ground-mount systems is very likely accurate, static company policy and is a legitimate thing for a setter to disclose. But immediately following it with 'we'll primarily focus on that Northern building' is the rep making a siting/design decision on the customer's multi-acre property — that part is premature and belongs to the specialist.
